mcqs.question: An object is placed beyond twice the focal length (2F) of a convex lens. Which ray diagram correctly shows the position and nature of the image formed?

options.A: Image formed between F and 2F, inverted, real, and smaller than the object.
options.B: Image formed at 2F, upright, virtual, and same size as the object.
options.C: Image formed beyond 2F, inverted, real, and larger than the object.

mcqs.answer: Image formed between F and 2F, inverted, real, and smaller than the object.
mcqs.explanation: For a convex lens, when the object is placed beyond 2F, the image is formed between the focal point (F) and twice the focal length (2F) on the opposite side. The image is real, inverted and reduced in size. Option A matches these properties; the other options describe incorrect positions or natures.

mcqs.question: A concave lens of focal length –15 cm forms an image of a candle placed 30 cm from the lens. Where is the image formed and what is its nature?

options.A: Image forms 10 cm on the same side as the object, virtual, upright, and reduced.
options.B: Image forms 20 cm on the opposite side, real, inverted, and enlarged.
options.C: Image forms at the focal point, real, inverted, and same size.

mcqs.answer: Image forms 10 cm on the same side as the object, virtual, upright, and reduced.
mcqs.explanation: Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v – 1/u with sign convention (u = –30 cm, f = –15 cm) gives 1/v = –1/10, so v = –10 cm. Negative v indicates a virtual image on the same side as the object, upright and smaller. Option A correctly states this; the other options are inconsistent with the calculation.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a convex lens from a concave lens?

options.A: A convex lens converges parallel rays to a real focus; a concave lens diverges rays as if they originated from a virtual focus.
options.B: A convex lens diverges rays; a concave lens converges rays.
options.C: Both lenses converge rays, but a convex lens has a longer focal length.
options.D: Both lenses diverge rays, but a concave lens has a shorter focal length.

mcqs.answer: A convex lens converges parallel rays to a real focus; a concave lens diverges rays as if they originated from a virtual focus.
mcqs.explanation: Convex (converging) lenses bring parallel incident rays to a real focal point on the opposite side. Concave (diverging) lenses cause rays to spread out as if they originated from a virtual focal point on the same side as the object. Option A captures this fundamental difference; the other options invert or misstate the behavior.

mcqs.question: In a thin convex lens, a ray passes through a point O of the lens without changing direction. Which point is O?

options.A: The geometric centre of the lens.

mcqs.answer: The geometric centre of the lens.
mcqs.explanation: The optical centre of a thin lens is the point at its geometric centre where a ray passes undeviated. This is a characteristic property of thin lenses. Hence option A is correct; the other points are distinct locations with different optical roles.

mcqs.question: A converging lens has a focal length of 12 cm. Where is its principal focus located?

options.A: 12 cm from the optical centre on the side opposite the object.
options.B: 12 cm from the optical centre on the same side as the object.
options.C: At the centre of the lens.

mcqs.answer: 12 cm from the optical centre on the side opposite the object.
mcqs.explanation: For a convex (converging) lens, the principal focus (real focus) lies on the side opposite the incoming light, at a distance equal to the focal length from the optical centre. Therefore option A is correct; option B describes the virtual focus of a concave lens, while C and D are unrelated.

mcqs.question: A thin converging lens forms a sharp image of a distant tree on a screen placed 20 cm behind the lens. What is the focal length of the lens?
mcqs.explanation: When the object is at a very large distance (practically at infinity), the image is formed at the focal plane of a converging lens. Hence the distance between the lens and the screen equals the focal length, which is 20 cm. Option A is correct; the other values do not satisfy the condition.

mcqs.question: A student draws a ray from the top of an object that passes through the focal point on the image side of a convex lens and then draws it emerging parallel to the principal axis. Is this construction correct?

options.A: Yes, because a ray passing through the focal point on the image side emerges parallel to the principal axis.
options.B: No, a ray passing through the focal point on the image side emerges through the focal point on the object side, not parallel.
options.C: No, a ray passing through the focal point on the object side emerges through the focal point on the image side, not parallel.
options.D: Yes, all rays that pass through any focal point become parallel after refraction.

mcqs.answer: No, a ray passing through the focal point on the image side emerges through the focal point on the object side, not parallel.
mcqs.explanation: For a convex lens, a ray that is parallel to the principal axis before reaching the lens passes through the focal point on the image side after refraction. Conversely, a ray that passes through the focal point on the object side emerges parallel to the principal axis. Therefore a ray entering through the focal point on the image side will not emerge parallel; it will diverge as if coming from the focal point on the object side. Option B correctly identifies the misconception; the other options state incorrect ray‑lens behavior.

mcqs.question: An object is placed at the focal point of a convex lens. What is the nature and position of the image formed?

options.A: Image formed at infinity, real, highly diminished.
options.B: Image formed at the focal point on the opposite side, virtual, upright, same size.
options.C: Image formed at twice the focal length, real, inverted, same size.

mcqs.answer: Image formed at infinity, real, highly diminished.
mcqs.explanation: When an object is placed exactly at the focal point of a convex lens, the refracted rays emerge parallel on the other side, never converging to a finite point. Hence the image is formed at infinity, is real (since the rays actually travel to infinity), and appears highly diminished. Option A captures this; options B, C, and D describe situations that occur for different object positions.
